faq.q: What is the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA)?
faq.a: FEMA is an Indian law that regulates all transactions involving foreign exchange, helping to manage foreign trade and payments. It ensures that money moving in and out of India is done according to approved guidelines.

It refers to an online business model where the e-commerce entity owns and stores the products it sells. When a customer places an order, the product is shipped directly from the entity's own stock or warehouse.

faq.q: Does this new rule apply to imported goods sold from India?
faq.a: No, this specific amendment applies only to "goods or products manufactured or produced in India" that are being exported. It does not change rules for selling imported goods within India.

faq.q: Will this help small businesses and artisans in India?
faq.a: Yes, it is expected to provide greater flexibility and a clearer regulatory framework for Indian manufacturers and e-commerce businesses, especially smaller ones, to use online platforms to sell their products to overseas markets.

faq.q: What other rules do businesses still need to follow?
faq.a: Businesses must still comply with India's overall Foreign Trade Policy 2023, the Handbook of Procedures (HBP), and the Foreign Exchange Management (Export of Goods & Services) Regulations, 2015, among others.
